title: pivot — gold spreads month across columns, pred lists it down the rows
gold_sql:
SELECT account_name,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = '1' THEN amount END) AS "1month",
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2' THEN amount END) AS "2month",
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = '3' THEN amount END) AS "3month"
  FROM journal
 GROUP BY account_name
pred_sql:
SELECT account_name, month, SUM(amount) AS amount
  FROM journal
 GROUP BY account_name, month
pred_csv:
account_name,month,amount
sales,1,100
sales,2,120
sales,3,90
purchase,1,40
purchase,2,50
purchase,3,45

title: pivot — the gold writes it as FILTER, not CASE WHEN
gold_sql:
SELECT account_name,
       SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE month = '1') AS "1month",
       SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE month = '2') AS "2month",
       SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE month = '3') AS "3month"
  FROM journal
 GROUP BY account_name
pred_sql: SELECT account_name, month, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY account_name, month
pred_csv:
account_name,month,amount
sales,1,100
sales,2,120
sales,3,90
purchase,1,40
purchase,2,50
purchase,3,45

title: pivot — the pivot lives in a CTE and the outer query only reads it
gold_sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT account_name,
         SUM(CASE WHEN month = '1' THEN amount END) AS "1month",
         SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2' THEN amount END) AS "2month"
    FROM journal
   GROUP BY account_name
)
SELECT account_name, "1month", "2month" FROM monthly
pred_sql:
SELECT account_name, month, SUM(amount) AS amount
  FROM journal
 GROUP BY account_name, month

title: row coverage — only the gold carries a total row
gold_sql: SELECT COALESCE(dept, 'TOTAL') AS dept, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept)
pred_sql: SELECT dept, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY dept

title: row coverage — both sides carry a total row, labelled differently (COALESCE vs GROUPING)
gold_sql:
SELECT COALESCE(dept, 'TOTAL') AS dept, SUM(amount) AS amount
  FROM journal
 GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept)
pred_sql:
SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(dept) = 1 THEN 'ALL' ELSE dept END AS dept, SUM(amount) AS amount
  FROM journal
 GROUP BY ROLLUP(dept)

title: row coverage — a subtotal row GROUPING SETS declared, present only in the gold
gold_sql:
SELECT dept, account_name, SUM(amount) AS amount
  FROM journal
 GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((dept, account_name), (dept))
pred_sql:
SELECT dept, account_name, SUM(amount) AS amount
  FROM journal
 GROUP BY dept, account_name

title: row coverage — the gold appends its total row by hand, as a UNION ALL branch
gold_sql:
SELECT dept, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY dept
UNION ALL
SELECT 'TOTAL', SUM(amount) FROM journal
pred_sql: SELECT dept, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY dept

title: row coverage, refused — a region code ('ALL') that looks like a total, but the SQL declares no total row
gold_sql: SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY region
pred_sql: SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE region <> 'ALL' GROUP BY region

title: grain — gold groups by account+account_no, pred by account. The measure is additive (sales)
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY account_code, account_no
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY account_code

title: grain — an average. The finer side carries the SUM and the COUNT it can be rebuilt from
gold_sql: SELECT branch, month, SUM(amount) AS TOTAL, COUNT(amount) AS cnt, AVG(amount) AS avg FROM journal GROUP BY branch, month
pred_sql: SELECT branch, AVG(amount) AS avg FROM journal GROUP BY branch

title: grain — a balance folded along the time axis. The numbers add up and mean nothing
gold_sql: SELECT accounts, month, SUM(balance) AS balance FROM balances GROUP BY accounts, month
pred_sql: SELECT accounts, SUM(balance) AS balance FROM balances GROUP BY accounts

title: different row counts, but not a roll-up — the pred excluded rows with a WHERE
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal GROUP BY account_code
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE amount >= 50 GROUP BY account_code

title: semi-additive, refused — the folded key is a year held as an integer, and its name says nothing
gold_sql: SELECT account, fy, SUM(balance) AS balance FROM balances GROUP BY account, fy
pred_sql: SELECT account, SUM(balance) AS balance FROM balances GROUP BY account

title: semi-additive, decided — the folded key is an integer too, but no period encoding fits it
gold_sql: SELECT branch, account_id, SUM(balance) AS balance FROM balances GROUP BY branch, account_id
pred_sql: SELECT branch, SUM(balance) AS balance FROM balances GROUP BY branch

title: re-aggregate COUNT(*) — the finer side is aggregated too, so the counts add
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: re-aggregate COUNT(column) — the finer side is raw rows, not an aggregate
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, COUNT(amount) AS cnt FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: re-aggregate AVG — the finer side is raw rows, so it is the mean of the rows
gold_sql: SELECT branch, amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025
pred_sql: SELECT branch, AVG(amount) AS avg FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY branch

title: re-aggregate MIN/MAX — additivity is not the question for these
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, MIN(amount) AS min_amount, MAX(amount) AS max_amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, MIN(amount) AS min_amount, MAX(amount) AS max_amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: re-aggregate SUM(a)/SUM(b) — numerator and denominator must both be on the finer side
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(profit_amount) AS profit, SUM(sales_amount) AS sales FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(profit_amount) / SUM(sales_amount) AS margin_rate FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: additivity — a non-additive measure (margin rate) folds along no axis at all
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(margin_rate) AS margin_rate FROM metrics WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(margin_rate) AS margin_rate FROM metrics WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: additivity — undeclared, the default. Before anyone authors the catalog every SUM lands here
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(qty) AS qty FROM inventory WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(qty) AS qty FROM inventory WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: refused — HAVING. A post-aggregate filter may already have dropped rows from the finer side
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no HAVING SUM(amount) > 30
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: refused — the joins differ. Re-adding fanned-out rows would pass a double count
gold_sql: SELECT l.account_code, l.account_no, SUM(l.amount) AS amount FROM journal l JOIN accounts a ON a.account_no = l.account_no WHERE l.year = 2025 GROUP BY l.account_code, l.account_no
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: refused — a window function. A per-row result is not something to add up again
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY account_code) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: refused — SELECT DISTINCT. Duplicates are already gone, so the original row count is unknown
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT account_code, account_no FROM journal WHERE year = 2025
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: refused — COUNT(DISTINCT). Summing the parts does not give the whole
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, COUNT(DISTINCT customer) AS customer_cnt FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, COUNT(DISTINCT customer) AS customer_cnt FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: grain direction — the pred is the finer of the two (PRED_FINER)
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no

title: CTE — the aggregate is inside the CTE and the outer query only reads it
gold_sql: WITH agg AS (SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no) SELECT account_code, account_no, amount FROM agg ORDER BY account_code, account_no
pred_sql: WITH agg AS (SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code) SELECT account_code, amount FROM agg ORDER BY account_code

title: derived table — the body, not the name, is what identifies the underlying row set
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, amount FROM (SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no) t ORDER BY 1, 2
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, amount FROM (SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code) t ORDER BY 1

title: CTE — a condition applied on top of an aggregated CTE. Still undecidable
gold_sql: WITH agg AS (SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no) SELECT account_code, account_no, amount FROM agg WHERE amount > 30
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: refused — SELECT * somewhere that is not a pass-through
gold_sql: SELECT * FROM journal WHERE year = 2025
pred_sql: SELECT account_code, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code

title: ratio, decided — strip the literal scale (x100) and re-aggregate
gold_sql: SELECT account_code, account_no, SUM(profit_amount) AS profit, SUM(sales_amount) AS sales FROM journal WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY account_code, account_no
